name: xTool D1 Pro 5W
tagline: 5W engraving-first module on xTool's open-frame D1 Pro rail
tldr: The 5W D1 Pro module is xTool's engraving-first head on the open-frame D1 rail: fine marks on wood, leather, and coated metal with occasional thin cuts. Swap to 10W–40W modules later on the same chassis.

priceRange.note: 5W optical module: verify SKU before buying

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

cannot: Clear acrylic cutting (diode light passes through)

pros: Fine spot (about 0.06 mm) for detailed photo and line engraving
Lowest price of the D1 Pro modules, especially on the used market
Large 430 × 390 mm frame for big engraving jobs at a small-laser price
cons: Cutting stops at card and about 3 mm basswood in several passes
Slow fills: about 25–36 min for a 10 × 10 cm photo in our benchmark
Discontinued: buy used, and check parts availability first
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 5W SKU on xTool D1 Pro. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other modules via the chips before buying.
proTips: Optimize for engraving: lower DPI on photos, higher scan speed on line art after test burns. Air assist still helps clarity. Compare benchmark times on the next module before assuming you need more power.
mainObjective: Detailed engraving on organics and coated metal: occasional thin cuts only

moduleSystem.headline: Swappable diode modules on D1 Pro frame
moduleSystem.description: xTool D1 Pro uses plug-in diode modules (5W–40W depending on era and listing). Buy the module power you need: same rail and software as other D1 Pro heads.

editorialDepth.advantages: The 5W diode module on xTool D1 Pro is right when you mostly engrave wood, leather, and slate and should not pay for cut watts you will not use weekly. Same chassis, upgrade path later.
editorialDepth.limitations: Skip this module if you cut 3 mm+ stock daily: open the 10W, 20W or 40W profile. Cast acrylic and bare metal without spray stay frustrating on diode.

faq.question: What can the D1 Pro 5W cut?
faq.answer: Very little: paper, card, felt and up to about 3 mm basswood in several passes, per our materials list. A 10 × 10 cm square in 3 mm basswood took about 15–22 min in our benchmark. It is an engraving module.

faq.question: Is a D1 Pro 5W still worth buying?
faq.answer: The D1 Pro line is discontinued, so the 5W is a used purchase. Well below the $499–$699 it sold for new, it is a capable fine-detail engraver on a large 430 × 390 mm frame. Check the module, belts and focus before buying, and confirm that spare parts are still available.

faq.question: D1 Pro 5W or 10W?
faq.answer: Choose the 5W only for engraving (photos on wood, leather, coated metal) at the lowest price. If you want to cut 3–5 mm plywood for ornaments or boxes, the 10W is much quicker (17–24 min against 25–36 min for a 10 × 10 cm photo in our benchmark) and typically cost about $100 more new.

standoutFeatures.title: Made for detail
standoutFeatures.body: With a spot of about 0.06 mm, the 5W head draws fine lines and photo dithering cleanly on wood, leather and coated metal.

standoutFeatures.title: Large frame, low cost
standoutFeatures.body: The D1 Pro frame offers 430 × 390 mm of work area, which a used 5W unit brings at a fraction of the price of newer machines.
